global: All critical JSON schemas are closed-world: exact key set, exact types, explicit nullable fields, unknown keys rejected.
Parsing rejects duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, NaN, Infinity, out-of-range integers, and non-canonical path spellings.
Canonical hashing uses one frozen JCS/RFC8785-compatible UTF-8 profile and published vectors.
Every sha256 is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; every event hash excludes only event_sha256 itself.
Every transaction-bound object binds transaction_id, contract_sha256, and schema/version.
Every mutable-path field is a normalized root-relative POSIX path; absolute paths, dot segments, parent traversal, backslashes, aliases, and symlink-resolved divergence are rejected.
Every critical enum is closed; unknown critical enum values fail closed and cannot derive PASS.

invariants: schema equals critical_apply.semantic_paths.v1
journal_segments is a non-empty ordered list of registered relative paths or a closed registered segment pattern with fixed bounds
all transaction-local paths resolve beneath bound root_realpath on root_device without symlink traversal
authority_db and witness_db are explicit external Linux-filesystem paths and may not alias transaction-local paths or each other
the byte-identical object hash is bound in CONTRACT-SEAL and passed to supervisor, reducer, checker, watcher, compatibility projector, and completion checker
no consumer may add defaults, discover alternatives, scan recursively, or reconstruct a path from argv
exactly one entry per normalized mutable path and exactly one creator_role and writer_role per entry
directory ownership and leaf ownership are separate entries; creating a child does not grant authority to recreate its parent
variant_guard is required for mutually exclusive fixture/live writers and is verified before launch
two entries resolving to the same device/inode or normalized path cause HOLD_DUPLICATE_MUTABLE_PATH_OWNERSHIP
unregistered mutable write or mkdir causes HOLD_UNREGISTERED_MUTABLE_PATH
ownership closure is checked statically from launch package and dynamically with write receipts
supervisor epoch exists and is journal committed before row creation
journal_sequence and journal_event_sha256 are null only in RESERVED_PENDING_JOURNAL
ACTIVE or CONSUMED requires a matching verified canonical journal event and current fencing token
RELEASE_PENDING requires a committed release-intent event
RELEASED is monotonic and cannot return to ACTIVE
unique constraints cover scope_or_nonce_sha256 and authority receipt identity as appropriate
AuthorityDB contains no semantic PASS/HOLD/FAIL/ABORT column

nullability: reservation journal fields null only while RESERVED_PENDING_JOURNAL
call_start fields non-null from CALL_START_COMMITTED onward except no-call retirement
outcome fields non-null only for OUTCOME_RECORDED or RETIRED after recorded outcome
UNKNOWN_CONSUMED requires call_start fields and forbids retry authority
RETIRED is final and durable even when semantic validation HOLDs

invariants: proposal_sha256 is computed over the canonical exact object
role/event allowlist and peer process identity are verified before acceptance
event_id uniqueness is resolved from the verified journal, never solely from ProgressDB
committer role is supervisor and binds full process identity
proposer and committer identities are distinct fields even when supervisor proposes
sequence begins at one and increments exactly by one
previous_event_sha256 equals prior canonical event hash or frozen genesis hash
critical ACK occurs only after complete append and fdatasync of journal bytes
checkpoint and ProgressDB publication are post-commit caches
semantic_input_closed is true
freeze_sequence and freeze_event_sha256 identify this committed fence/head
allowed post-freeze types are a closed allowlist of closeout-only events
semantic evidence proposed after ACK of the fence is rejected
recovery reruns the same reducer over the same frozen prefix

authority: CONSUMED -> RELEASE_PENDING when releasable scope; consumed nonce instead follows nonce machine
nonce: COMMITTED_NOT_USED -> RETIRED for explicit no-call retirement
UNKNOWN_CONSUMED -> RETIRED only as non-retryable retirement under a new journal event
illegal: protected action while authority row is pending, journal-committed-but-not-active, mismatched, released, or unknown
provider/protected call before durable CALL_START_COMMITTED acknowledgement
retry after CALL_START_COMMITTED without recorded outcome
semantic event after terminal input fence
terminal decision before cleanup or without committed fence
semantic terminal regression or second different terminal decision
protected action after scope release intent
closed journal append for a late notification receipt
PASS seal while owned process state is not CLEAN

crash_matrix.boundary: before supervisor epoch journal commit
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no AuthorityDB row may exist; fresh epoch required

crash_matrix.boundary: after supervisor epoch commit before AuthorityDB reserve
crash_matrix.required_recovery: epoch reusable only under same recovered supervisor policy; no scope authority exists

crash_matrix.boundary: after AuthorityDB RESERVED_PENDING_JOURNAL commit before journal reserve event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: row cannot authorize; deterministically abandon/release or complete matching journal reservation under current fence

crash_matrix.boundary: during journal reserve append before fdatasync
crash_matrix.required_recovery: torn/unacknowledged tail quarantined; row remains non-authorizing pending

crash_matrix.boundary: after journal reserve fdatasync before AuthorityDB binds sequence/hash
crash_matrix.required_recovery: verify exact event then bind row; mismatch HOLD

crash_matrix.boundary: after row JOURNAL_COMMITTED before ACTIVE
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no protected action; promote only after journal binding and fence verification

crash_matrix.boundary: after ACTIVE before protected barrier event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: scope held but action forbidden until barrier; resume or release per frozen policy

crash_matrix.boundary: after release intent journal commit before DB RELEASE_PENDING
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no further protected action; complete release

crash_matrix.boundary: after DB RELEASED before journal release-recorded event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: append matching release-recorded event; never reactivate

crash_matrix.boundary: after journal release-recorded before supervisor close
crash_matrix.required_recovery: complete closeout; scope remains released

crash_matrix.boundary: before nonce row reserve
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no nonce authority

crash_matrix.boundary: after nonce RESERVED_PENDING_JOURNAL before reservation event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no call; complete exact reservation or retire without call

crash_matrix.boundary: after reservation event before COMMITTED_NOT_USED row binding
crash_matrix.required_recovery: bind exact event; no call until state commit

crash_matrix.boundary: COMMITTED_NOT_USED before call-start event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: safe resume only under same valid frozen authority and proof no call-start event

crash_matrix.boundary: during call-start journal append before durable ACK
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no call may have been invoked by contract; recover journal prefix and remain non-used or retire

crash_matrix.boundary: after CALL_START_COMMITTED durable ACK before invocation
crash_matrix.required_recovery: default UNKNOWN_CONSUMED, non-retryable; conservative false consumption is allowed

crash_matrix.boundary: during or after external invocation before response
crash_matrix.required_recovery: UNKNOWN_CONSUMED; new owner authority and new nonce required for any later attempt

crash_matrix.boundary: response received before durable outcome event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: UNKNOWN_CONSUMED unless the same response bytes were durably CAS-bound and exact outcome event recovery is proven; never retry

crash_matrix.boundary: outcome journaled before AuthorityDB OUTCOME_RECORDED bind
crash_matrix.required_recovery: bind exact outcome and retire

crash_matrix.boundary: OUTCOME_RECORDED before RETIRED
crash_matrix.required_recovery: retire idempotently; semantic HOLD does not unconsume

crash_matrix.boundary: journal full line written before fdatasync
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no ACK; valid prefix or quarantined tail only

crash_matrix.boundary: journal fdatasync after full event before ACK
crash_matrix.required_recovery: journal-derived idempotency returns original ACK on retry; no duplicate append

crash_matrix.boundary: after ACK before ProgressDB/checkpoint update
crash_matrix.required_recovery: replay journal; original ACK and event preserved

crash_matrix.boundary: after TERMINAL_REDUCTION_PREPARED before reducer output
crash_matrix.required_recovery: rerun same reducer over same semantic_reduction_head

crash_matrix.boundary: after reduction publication before TERMINAL_DECISION
crash_matrix.required_recovery: verify reduction hash and append one decision or discard unbound output

crash_matrix.boundary: after TERMINAL_DECISION before seal
crash_matrix.required_recovery: replay decision, publish create-once manifest/seal

crash_matrix.boundary: after valid seal while status/progress says RUNNING
crash_matrix.required_recovery: terminal-first reconciliation reports sealed terminal and rebuilds stale projections

crash_matrix.boundary: CAS source opened then path replaced
crash_matrix.required_recovery: descriptor bytes and identity govern; replacement path ignored/detected

crash_matrix.boundary: CAS temp written before fdatasync
crash_matrix.required_recovery: orphan temp removable; no journal ACK

crash_matrix.boundary: CAS object published before parent fsync
crash_matrix.required_recovery: no journal ACK; revalidate or orphan

crash_matrix.boundary: CAS parent fsync before journal artifact event
crash_matrix.required_recovery: orphan immutable object allowed; no semantic reference

crash_matrix.boundary: journal artifact event ACK after CAS publication
crash_matrix.required_recovery: referenced object must re-open, rehash, and survive; absence is integrity HOLD

journal_only_semantic_authority_tests: Delete ProgressDB, checkpoint, all projections, and controller status; replay journal plus CAS and reproduce byte-identical semantic reduction.
Corrupt or forge ProgressDB terminal while journal is nonterminal; journal result wins and health HOLD records mismatch.
Forge projection RUNNING after valid sealed PASS/HOLD/FAIL/ABORT; checker reports sealed terminal and rebuilds projection.
Forge projection PASS without canonical terminal decision/seal; PASS is rejected.
Delete ProgressDB after ACK, retry same event_id and proposal hash; original ACK is returned without append.
Corrupt ProgressDB idempotency row then retry; journal map is reconstructed before decision.
Retry event_id with different proposal hash; canonical integrity conflict is committed/emergency-recorded and PASS blocked.
Put semantic_result in AuthorityDB or WitnessDB fixture; reducer ignores it and schema gate rejects authority-store semantic fields.
Mutate original worker artifact after CAS capture; reduction remains identical from CAS.
Mutate unregistered artifact path; reducer ignores it and launch/write gate records violation.
Delete compatibility harness status and registry rows; terminal truth remains unchanged.
Truncate journal behind independently witnessed head; WitnessDB detects mismatch and trustworthy closeout HOLDs without inventing semantics.
descriptor_bound_cas_tests: open registered source relative to verified directory FD with O_NOFOLLOW/openat2 equivalent
reject ancestor and leaf symlink swaps
reject unexpected st_nlink greater than one unless contract explicitly allows and binds it
bind and compare device, inode, uid, gid, mode, size, ctime/mtime policy before and after stream copy
hash and copy through one opened source descriptor with no path reopen
concurrent source truncation, extension, overwrite, chmod, chown, rename, replacement, and hardlink injection all fail closed or bind original stable descriptor bytes
same-filesystem O_EXCL temporary publication, complete writes, fdatasync, no-overwrite atomic publish, and parent fsync
reopen published object with O_NOFOLLOW and rehash before journal append
duplicate hash publication is accepted only after existing object reopens and hashes identically
CAS object modes and owner are fixed; later mutation attempt detected
orphan unreferenced objects never become semantic evidence through scanning
sqlite_wal_gates: AuthorityDB and WitnessDB reside on a proven Linux local filesystem, never /mnt/c or unproven network/storage semantics.
Database creation is followed by file sync and parent-directory fsync before authority use.
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL is set and the returned mode is asserted; PRAGMA synchronous=FULL is set and asserted.
PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, trusted_schema=OFF where supported, fixed application_id, and exact user_version/schema migration checks are asserted.
Lease/nonce mutations use BEGIN IMMEDIATE, bounded busy_timeout, explicit commit, and fail-closed contention classification.
Unique constraints and CHECK constraints enforce state enums, nonce/scope uniqueness, and state-dependent journal binding nullability.
On startup run quick_check/integrity policy, validate WAL/SHM ownership/mode, and refuse authority on corruption or unrecognized schema.
Live backup uses SQLite backup API or a frozen checkpoint/quiesce protocol; copying only the main DB while WAL may contain rows is forbidden.
Recovery and restore include main DB, -wal, and -shm as one protocol, or prove a completed checkpoint with exclusive/quiescent ownership.
Crash tests cover before/after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, row write, WAL sync, COMMIT, checkpoint, backup, restore, and journal cross-store boundaries.
WitnessDB assurance is frozen as WITNESS_GRADE_1_SAME_HOST_SAME_UID_INDEPENDENT_PROCESS_DETECTION and makes no hostile same-UID prevention claim.
ProgressDB may use weaker rebuildable policy only if its indexed journal head is verified before acceleration and deletion remains safe.

r18_findings.finding: nonce-ledger directory has duplicate creator ownership
r18_findings.evidence: materializer creates nonce-ledger with mkdir(exist_ok=True); live runner later calls ledger_root.mkdir(mode=0o700) without exist_ok; historical RUN-RESULT records [Errno 17] File exists
r18_findings.required_repair: register exactly one directory creator. Recommended M0 architecture: Authority service creates/owns AuthorityDB nonce storage; transaction components submit operations and never mkdir/write the store. If legacy R18 remains for migration, materializer alone creates the directory and runner only validates registered identity/mode, never creates it.

r18_findings.finding: per-run nonce ledger is not sufficient cross-transaction authority
r18_findings.evidence: broker locks and writes nonce-ledger/nonce-ledger.json beneath one run root; uniqueness is local to that root
r18_findings.required_repair: move nonce authority and replay exclusion to AuthorityDB with one service/library owner and journal-bound fenced transitions

r18_findings.finding: fixture and live runner both claim the same ledger leaf under alternate code paths without a frozen variant ownership contract
r18_findings.evidence: synthetic runner directly writes nonce-ledger/nonce-ledger.json; live broker publishes the same leaf
r18_findings.required_repair: either remove both in favor of AuthorityDB or freeze mutually exclusive variant_guard and prove only one selected writer before launch

r18_findings.finding: valid terminal HOLD coexists with stale harness RUNNING projections
r18_findings.evidence: semantic STATUS is terminal HOLD at 23:47:09Z and TERMINAL-SEAL declares terminal HOLD; harness status remains RUNNING from 23:46:00Z and progress says RUNNING/reconcile_semantic_terminal at 23:47:09Z
r18_findings.required_repair: terminal-first resolution must report HOLD, classify the RUNNING files as stale rebuildable projections, publish reconciled projections atomically, and never alter the sealed terminal

stale_projection_reconciliation_gates: Resolve exact registered terminal seal path first; verify create-once seal, manifest, terminal decision, reduction, and journal bindings.
If valid sealed terminal exists, return semantic result immediately regardless of PID, heartbeat, harness registry, observer status, or RUNNING projection.
Classify each conflicting projection with observed hash, bound head, staleness reason, and replacement receipt.
Rebuild projection solely from journal/CAS and atomically replace only supervisor-owned projection paths.
Never mutate journal, seal, reduction, manifest, or semantic result during projection repair.
If no valid terminal exists, verify supervisor lock plus full process identity and same-boot monotonic lease; projection alone never establishes RUNNING.
After rebuild, independent checker repeats terminal-first resolution and proves parity.
Regression fixture uses the hashed R18 HOLD seal plus stale RUNNING status/progress observations.
likely_implementation_hazards: Current critical_apply_authority.py explicitly says the consumption marker is authoritative and journal append is best-effort; this violates journal-only transaction fact authority and B1.
Current consumption reconciliation searches raw journal text for approval_consumed rather than validating an exact event schema, transaction, nonce, sequence, and hash binding.
Current journal event v2 lacks event_id, proposal hash, contract hash, supervisor epoch, proposer/committer split, CAS artifact refs, and role allowlist required by the owner revision.
Current JournalWriterToken is ordinary caller-supplied data and append_event does not itself prove held supervisor flock, current epoch, fencing token, or authenticated ingress role.

Current journal validation treats journal-head.json as the committed offset authority; the frozen design says journal bytes are canonical and checkpoint/head is rebuildable. Recovery semantics must not lose a durably acknowledged line because a derived head update failed.
Current idempotency has no journal-derived event_id map; ProgressDB-safe duplicate ACK behavior is absent.
Current rehydration derives state from receipt/path presence and may write generation/rehydration receipts before terminal-first seal resolution; this risks treating derived files as authority.
Current controller query is a file-presence view and does not perform terminal-first journal/reduction verification.
Current observer-status and worker-result files can remain stale; no canonical stale-projection reconciliation contract is implemented.
Current terminal seal does not bind semantic_reduction_head, terminal_decision_head, closeout_head, reducer, reduction, contract, or cleanup event as required.
Current manifest hashes paths by reopening them and uses replace publication; this is TOCTOU-prone and not descriptor-bound create-once CAS publication.
No current critical_apply CAS module implements openat/O_NOFOLLOW descriptor capture and publication durability ordering.
No current AuthorityDB/ProgressDB/WitnessDB module freezes SQLite/WAL authority-grade settings and recovery/backup semantics.
No immutable semantic-path registration and complete mutable-path ownership registry is present in current source.

Current transition table predates terminal fence/three-head vocabulary and does not encode notification, independent witness, AuthorityDB release, completion receipt, supervisor close, then lock-release ordering.
Creating directories with exist_ok=True in multiple components can hide duplicate ownership instead of proving it absent.
Same-UID checker/WitnessDB claims can be overstated unless assurance grade is explicit.
A late notification callback must not append to a closed journal; current adapters need an explicit follow-up evidence policy.

Crash recovery across two durable authorities can accidentally create a second semantic authority if reconciliation chooses DB state over journal fact rather than using DB only to gate cross-transaction authority.
single_owner_nonce_repair_acceptance: One registered owner creates AuthorityDB directory, database, WAL, SHM, schema, scope rows, and nonce rows.
Supervisor never writes AuthorityDB files directly; it invokes the authority API/library under fencing and journals returned receipt hashes.
Workers, runners, brokers, checkers, materializers, reducers, and compatibility projectors have zero write/mkdir authority for nonce storage.
Independent checker reads through read-only authority API/snapshot and writes only checker receipts/WitnessDB.
Legacy nonce-ledger path is absent in new transactions or registered read-only migration input; its presence as mutable live authority blocks launch.
Static ownership closure and dynamic write audit both prove one creator/writer and no aliases.
